title: Zigbee network has severe outbound delays after Home Assistant Core updates
body: Since updating Home Assistant Core from 2022.9.0 to 2022.9.1, my ZHA network has become extremely slow. Turning a light on or off can take more than 30 seconds or fail entirely. I am running Home Assistant OS with a zzh coordinator. The log contains zigpy-znp request timeouts and CancelledError/TimeoutError exceptions.

symptoms_visible: On Home Assistant Core 2022.9.1, turning a Zigbee light on or off can take more than 30 seconds or may not work at all.
The log shows zigpy-znp requests ending in CancelledError and TimeoutError.
N0.label: N0 severe Zigbee delay reported

symptoms_visible: After downgrading to 2022.9.0, my Zigbee devices respond normally.
After subsequently installing 2022.9.2, the network initially responds normally again.
N1.label: N1 version-dependent behavior observed

symptoms_visible: The problem is intermittent, and after installing 2022.9.4 the long Zigbee delays return.
N2.label: N2 intermittent delay recurs

symptoms_visible: During an affected period, light commands remain delayed or unresponsive and the log repeatedly contains AttributeError saying 'NoneType' has no attribute 'request_callback_rsp'.
N3.label: N3 coordinator communication errors collected

symptoms_visible: My Zigbee motion and door sensors update immediately, but commands sent to lights are delayed or unresponsive at the same time.
A light command may execute one to five minutes after I send it.
Other affected setups also receive sensor events normally while commands from the hub to bulbs or switches are delayed.
N4.label: N4 directional traffic pattern established

symptoms_visible: With Bluetooth disabled, commands work somewhat better on one affected setup but are still slower than before.
The same Zigbee lag also occurs on another affected setup where Bluetooth was already disabled.
N4_x.label: N4_x Bluetooth-disable aftermath

symptoms_visible: After updating to Home Assistant Core 2022.10.2, Zigbee commands work again without the long delay.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved after Core update

symptoms_visible: After updating to Home Assistant Core 2022.10.2, Zigbee commands work again without the long delay.
N_terminal_bt.label: terminal resolved after partial Bluetooth workaround

question_patterns: Does the network return to normal if you reinstall the last working Core version?
Can you confirm whether the delay follows the Core version?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I went back to 2022.9.0 and it is working normally. This is only broken for me on the newer build.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The network is just as slow after going back to 2022.9.0.
It returns to normal after downgrading, but only after one additional restart.

question_patterns: What happens if you install the next maintenance update and test the same lights?
Does the issue still occur on the newer Core build?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: On 2022.9.2 it initially seems fixed. My lights are responding normally again, although I want to wait and see because the problem has been intermittent.

edges.comment: The reporter tested multiple installed Core versions. These persistent version changes receive distinct system states even though the tests primarily collect evidence.

question_patterns: Has the improvement remained stable after further use or another update?
Does the delay recur on the latest build?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It is off and on for me too. I upgraded to 2022.9.4 and the issue seems to be back.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The improvement has remained stable through later updates and the delay has not returned.

edges.comment: The temporary improvement on 2022.9.2 was not sufficient to close the technical investigation because the reporter later reproduced the delay on 2022.9.4.

question_patterns: Can you enable ZHA debug logging and share the complete errors from an affected period?
What does the ZHA log contain while commands are delayed?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: While it is happening, I get repeated errors from ZHA light state refreshes. The traceback ends in zigpy_znp with `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'request_callback_rsp'`; I saw dozens of occurrences.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The debug log is clean during the delay and shows successful outbound requests with acknowledgements.
The same traceback occurs fewer times during a shorter affected period.

question_patterns: What coordinator are you using, and how is it physically connected to the server?
Is the Zigbee stick on an extension cable or close to an access point?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I am using a zzh stick connected to my NUC through a two-foot USB extension cable. It is not near a Wi-Fi access point.

question_patterns: Is there a Bluetooth adapter or another USB device near the coordinator?
Which USB ports and hubs are being used around the Zigbee stick?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I have a Bluetooth adapter on a USB hub with its own two-foot cable from another USB port. All the ports are USB 3.0.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: There is no Bluetooth hardware and no other USB device attached to the server.

edges.comment: The raw traceback and physical layout are user-provided evidence. The maintainer's interpretation that this reflects a broken coordinator connection is not placed in the user's answer.

question_patterns: Are all Zigbee devices unresponsive, or do any sensor reports still arrive normally?
What happens to motion and door sensor events while the lights are delayed?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My motion and door sensors still update instantly. I can walk into a room and see the Zigbee motion sensor trigger in Home Assistant while the light that should turn on remains completely unresponsive.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Nothing works in either direction; sensor reports also stop completely whenever the lights stop responding.

question_patterns: Is there a difference between events coming from devices and commands sent to devices?
Can a delayed command eventually execute, and if so how long afterward?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It seems directional. Reports from devices reach Home Assistant normally, but commands from the hub to lights or switches are delayed. A command can execute a couple of minutes later, sometimes as much as five minutes later.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Commands are sent immediately, but Home Assistant only displays the resulting state several minutes later.

edges.comment: Reports from the original reporter and other affected users are folded into one simulated user side. The cross-user evidence includes zzh, RaspBee II, and other coordinator setups, with the shared directional symptom being more informative than the device brands.

solution.intent: Treat Bluetooth RF activity as the complete cause and disable Bluetooth on the host to resolve the Zigbee delay.
solution.concrete_example: Disable the host Bluetooth radio, reboot, and retest outbound Zigbee commands.

edges.comment: Disabling Bluetooth was actually tried. It produced only partial improvement on one affected setup, while another affected setup already had Bluetooth disabled and still reproduced the lag, so Bluetooth interference was not established as the complete case-wide explanation.

solution.intent: Treat this as an intermittent, release-correlated outbound Zigbee communication regression with no exact causal change established in the thread; update to a newer Core build and ask the user to verify bidirectional Zigbee behavior before declaring resolution.
solution.concrete_example: Update to the current Home Assistant Core release and retest both sensor events and commands to lights or switches. In the thread, affected users reported normal response after installing 2022.10.2, although no specific fixing changelog entry was identified.
solution.inference_hint: The evidence supports a directional coordinator-to-device transmission problem and a release-correlated recovery, but the thread never identifies the exact Core change that caused or fixed it. Bluetooth RF noise and serial disconnection were hypotheses, not a final universally accepted mechanism.

edges.comment: Shortcut for an agent that recommends the later fixed build without first repeating the partially effective Bluetooth experiment. Verification occurs terminal-side through the user's observation after updating.

solution.intent: After Bluetooth disabling proves incomplete, update to a newer Core build and verify that outbound Zigbee commands and inbound sensor reports both work normally before declaring resolution.
solution.concrete_example: Keep Bluetooth interference as a possible environmental contributor rather than the complete diagnosis, update Home Assistant Core, and retest. Affected users reported that 2022.10.2 restored normal Zigbee response without identifying a corresponding changelog item.
solution.inference_hint: The final thread evidence establishes recovery on a later Core build but not the identity or mechanism of the fixing change. The coexistence of immediate inbound sensor events and delayed outbound commands supports directional degradation; it does not prove Bluetooth interference or a permanent serial disconnection as the sole cause.

edges.comment: Canonical recovery after the in-thread Bluetooth experiment. Reports from affected users are merged; the unrelated gateway-pairing screenshots and a separate coordinator reflashing incident are deliberately excluded.

satisfaction_conditions: Must characterize the accepted diagnosis conservatively: the observed failure is an intermittent, release-correlated degradation of Zigbee traffic from the coordinator to devices, while inbound sensor reports can remain immediate; the thread does not establish the exact regressing or fixing code change.
Diagnosis must be grounded in the version-dependent behavior, repeated zigpy-znp communication errors, and the directional command-versus-sensor observations.
Must not present disabling Bluetooth as the complete fix: it only partially improved one affected setup, and another affected setup reproduced the delay with Bluetooth already disabled.
Must not generalize the separate user's coordinator-reflashing recovery or unrelated gateway-pairing problem as the solution to this case.

The final recommendation must be to update to a newer Core build that restores normal Zigbee response and ask the user to verify both outbound commands and inbound reports before treating the issue as resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Home Assistant user who can change Core versions, enable logging, inspect tracebacks, and describe USB and radio hardware, but does not claim to know the internal ZHA mechanism.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct and persistent; reports practical observations and challenges explanations that conflict with simultaneous sensor behavior. Other affected users are folded into the same user side for cross-hardware evidence.
